trigger: concurrency/ordering (3f-bis -> 3g sequencing across subagent spawns) + cross-module coupling (shared/scripts/lib <-> iterate campaign prose) + irreversible op (PR merge gate)

doubts.claim_under_doubt: 3f-bis, as written, carries a reviewed unit from pin to ship on the live path
doubts.disproof_attempt: campaign-mode.md 239-242 states the rule (state crosses steps in a FILE; a fresh Bash call has an empty environment) but 3f-bis breaks it internally. `run_dir` (243) and `pr_url` (245) are consumed at 365 (`echo "$shipped_head" > "$run_dir/reviewed_head"`) and 383 (`gh pr view "$pr_url"` / `cat "$run_dir/reviewed_head"`) AFTER three Agent-tool spawns (a/b/c) and several `record` calls -- necessarily different Bash calls. `diff_head`/`fires` (261-264) are consumed at 309/314, and `fires` requires the orchestrator to READ the diff and judge risk flags, so the pin call is realistically a separate Bash call too. Traced consequences with empty vars: `$diff_head` empty -> `[ sha = "" ] || STRICT-STOP` fires on EVERY unit (spurious stop); `$fires` empty -> `$([ "$fires" = "1" ] || echo --review-skipped)` passes `--review-skipped` for a unit the cascade then reviews -> pin.shipped_head=reviewed_head -> after the record commit is PUSHED, `--mode ship` refuses (`already has shipped_head`) -> STRICT-STOP post-push; `$run_dir` empty -> legacy overwrite goes to `/reviewed_head`, 3g pins `--match-head-commit <pre-record reviewed_head>` -> GitHub refuses the merge. Every branch is fail-closed for the merge, but the mechanism cannot complete a reviewed unit unless the orchestrator silently re-derives the variables the doc forbids relying on. No prose test covers intra-step variable lifetime (test_the_head_pin_crosses_steps_in_a_file_not_a_shell_variable only checks 3f-bis->3g).
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: In the post-cascade block re-derive `run_dir` and `pr_url` inline from template placeholders exactly as 3g already does (`run_dir="{project_root}/.shipwright/runs/{loop_id}/{id}"`; `pr_url=$(cd "{project_root}" && gh pr view "{branch}" --json url -q .url)`); persist `diff_head` and `fires` to `$run_dir/diff_head` / `$run_dir/fires` at compute time and `cat` them back at the pin call and the equality check; move the legacy-file overwrite INTO ship() (it already has project_root/loop_id/unit_id and only writes after its checks pass), deleting line 365 so `$run_dir` is not needed there at all. Add a prose test: every `$name` referenced after the `a) spec-reviewer` marker in 3f-bis is assigned after that marker too.
doubts.disposition: PARTIALLY ACCEPTED. `run_dir`/`pr_url` genuinely cross the a/b/c spawn boundary (defined line 243-246, first consumed post-spawn at line 361+) and are fixed this round by re-deriving both inline immediately before the post-cascade block, mirroring 3g's own existing pattern. `diff_head`/`fires`/`pin_json`, however, do NOT cross the spawn boundary on the current line numbers: the pin call (302-309) and the diff_head equality check (314) both run BEFORE the `a) spec-reviewer` marker at line 324 -- the disproof's own line references (309/314) are before, not after, 324. No fix applied for those three; the underlying single-Bash-block assumption for that portion of the step is correct as written.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: a Stage-2 finding can be 'addressed' at 3f-bis without producing a misattributed merge (code-review lows (a)+(c), assessed jointly and escalated)
doubts.disproof_attempt: Line 389 ('a Stage-2 high finding left unaddressed -> STRICT-STOP') tells the orchestrator addressing is allowed; the only way to address a code finding is a fix commit F on top of reviewed_head. The step then says record `completed` rows, `git commit` R, `git push` (363, ||STRICT-STOP passes), overwrite `$run_dir/reviewed_head` with R (365), THEN `--mode ship` (374-377) -- which now refuses because R^ == F != reviewed_head. Net state after that STRICT-STOP: origin/{branch} = reviewed_head+F+R with reviews.json on it saying every stage `completed` for a diff the reviewers never saw (F is unreviewed); review_pin.json.shipped_head = null; the legacy file = R. The doc says the PR is 'left OPEN so a human can repair it' -- a human resuming at 3g runs `--match-head-commit $(cat reviewed_head)` = R and merges the mixed reviewed/unreviewed tree with a green record on it: the exact misattribution class R3 exists to close, reached by following the doc's own prose. The automated loop is safe (STRICT-STOP never reaches 3g; a re-entry hits `rm -f` at 243), which is why each half was rated low in isolation; together, on the routine Stage-2-finding path, they steer into a post-push stop with a stale, rejected legacy pin.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: At 389 state plainly: addressing a finding means a NEW commit, which the `--mode ship` guard refuses by design -- go back to the top of 3f-bis (`rm -f`, re-diff, re-pin, re-run the cascade); never commit on top of the pinned tree and never record `completed` for a diff that has since changed. And swap the order at 365/374 (ship first, legacy write only on success) -- or, per doubt 1, let ship() own the legacy write. Add a prose test asserting the ship call precedes the legacy overwrite in 3f-bis.
doubts.disposition: ACCEPTED, fixed this round: line 389 now states addressing a finding means restarting 3f-bis from the top, never committing on top of the pinned tree; the ship call and the legacy-file write are reordered (ship validates first, `|| STRICT-STOP`; the legacy file is only written after ship succeeds), so a STRICT-STOPped ship never leaves a rejected SHA in the legacy file a human could resume against.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: ship()'s 'exactly one commit ahead of reviewed_head' check proves the shipped tree is the reviewed tree plus reviews.json (code-review low (b), escalated)
doubts.disproof_attempt: `git rev-parse {sha}^` (review_attribution.py:425, and :355 in verify) resolves the FIRST parent only, and the check is topology-only -- it never looks at what the one commit contains; the spec demoted `diff_sha256` to 'evidence, not a gate', so nothing content-level backs the sole live enforcement point. Concrete route on the pre-R5a SHARED worktree the runner and orchestrator both use: if that worktree carries a `MERGE_HEAD` (a resolved-but-uncommitted merge left behind -- e.g. a bring-branch-current step that died after conflict resolution), then 3f-bis's `git -C "{project_root}" add reviews.json && git commit -m ...` (361-362) silently produces a MERGE commit R whose first parent is reviewed_head and whose tree is the merge result; ship() ALLOWs (R^ == reviewed_head), verify() ALLOWs, 3g merges everything MERGE_HEAD carried, unreviewed. Simpler route, same class: `git add <one path>` adds to whatever is ALREADY staged in the index; any pre-staged entry rides along in R. 'Not reachable today' assumed a clean worktree state that a shared worktree does not guarantee.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: In ship() and verify(): replace `rev-parse {sha}^` with `git rev-list --parents -n 1 {sha}` and require exactly two tokens (one parent) equal to reviewed_head. Additionally let ship() take an optional `--only-path <reviews.json path>` (3f-bis knows it) and assert `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r {sha}` equals exactly that one path. Add two tests: a merge record commit (`git merge --no-commit <other>` then the record commit) and a record commit with a pre-staged extra file -- both must be refused.
doubts.disposition: PARTIALLY ACCEPTED. The merge-commit gap is real and fixed this round: ship() and verify() now use `git rev-list --parents -n 1 {sha}` and require exactly one parent, rejecting a merge record commit outright. The stronger `--only-path` content assertion is deferred: it requires threading the reviews.json path into ship()'s contract as a new parameter and changes what the function verifies (path-scoped, not just ancestry-scoped) -- a deliberate scope decision for a future sub-iterate (R4/R5b, both already chartered with the merge-lane/state-mechanics surface this touches), not silently dropped.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: 3f-bis/3g are 'already calling through' the per-unit resolver such that R5a changes only two call-site values (bloat-exception ADR, YAGNI, lines 117-120)
doubts.disproof_attempt: The pin/ship call site uses ONE placeholder for three distinct roots: the state root (`--state "{project_root}/.shipwright/loop_state.json"`), the evidence root (`--project-root "{project_root}"` -> `.shipwright/runs/`), and the git root (`diff_head`, `diff`, `git add/commit/push`, `rev-parse HEAD`, `--campaign-worktree`). campaign-mode.md 254-260 says `{project_root}` itself becomes per-unit under R5a; the ADR says R5a changes only `--project-root`/`--campaign-worktree`. Neither works: `.shipwright/*` is gitignored (.gitignore:155) so a fresh per-unit worktree has NO loop_state.json and no runs/ -- a per-unit `{project_root}` makes `_resolve` fail at `durable_read_text` (fail-closed, but R5a must rework the whole block); under the ADR's reading the `diff_head` line stays on the campaign worktree while pin() resolves HEAD in the unit worktree, so the inline equality check STRICT-STOPs every unit. Fail-closed both ways, so no live impact -- but the R5a-readiness claim this sub-iterate ships is not true as stated.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Introduce distinct placeholders now: `{campaign_worktree}` for `--state`, `--project-root`, `--campaign-worktree` and `run_dir`; `{unit_worktree}` (defined as = `{project_root}` today) for every `git -C` call in 3f-bis/3g. Correct the ADR's YAGNI paragraph to say R5a must supply `{unit_worktree}` and set the row's `worktree`, nothing else.
doubts.disposition: DEFERRED to R5a. This finding names exactly the work the doc already assigns R5a ('making `{project_root}` itself resolve to a genuine per-unit path is R5a's responsibility', campaign-mode.md line 258-260) -- introducing a second placeholder now, without R5a's actual per-unit worktree machinery to populate it, would be speculative. Recorded here so R5a's own dispatch inherits this exact finding rather than rediscovering it.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: ship()'s 'a re-ship after retry must not be silent' guard is enforceable
doubts.disproof_attempt: pin() overwrites `review_pin.json` unconditionally (test_review_attribution_probes.py:62 documents this as intended), including a pin whose `shipped_head` is set. The documented re-entry route (`rm -f` at 243, re-pin) therefore bypasses the overwrite guard by design -- re-pin, then ship, and the guard never sees the prior head -- and destroys the only evidence that a given diff was pinned and REJECTED (the Stage-1 REJECT path at 394-409 leaves that pin as the record of what was refused).
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Have pin() archive an existing pin (`review_pin.<pinned_at>.json`) before overwriting, or refuse to overwrite a pin whose `shipped_head` is non-null unless `--force`; document which.
doubts.disposition: DEFERRED to R4 (state mechanics). Pin lifecycle/archival policy across retries is a state-mechanics concern R4 is explicitly chartered to design holistically, not a one-off patch to `pin()` here; today's behavior is unchanged from round 1-3 (not a regression introduced by this round).

doubts.disproof_attempt: 3g's `gh pr merge ... $head_pin` (434) has no `|| STRICT-STOP` and is followed by an UNBOUNDED `until [ state = MERGED ]; do sleep 5; done` (435) -- the 'third outcome the loop has no name for' that 3f-bis's own wait was bounded to avoid. Likely pre-existing, but R3 deliberately raises the base rate of `--match-head-commit` refusals (every STRICT-STOP path now leaves a legacy file the remote no longer matches; doubts 1 and 2 add more), so a refused merge now spins forever instead of stopping. test_step_3f_bis_bounds_its_wait covers 3f-bis only.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: `gh pr merge ... || STRICT-STOP` and a `seq 1 N` cap on the MERGED wait; extend the bounded-wait prose test to step 3g.
doubts.disposition: ACCEPTED, fixed this round: `gh pr merge ... $head_pin || STRICT-STOP`, and the MERGED wait is now bounded with the same `seq 1 60` / sleep 5 pattern 3f-bis already uses, STRICT-STOPping if the cap is reached without observing MERGED.

summary: 0 high, 3 medium, 4 low (round 2 of doubt review). 5 of 7 findings fixed this round: run_dir/pr_url re-derivation across the a/b/c spawn boundary; the 'addressing a finding' prose corrected plus ship-before-legacy-write reordering; ship()/verify()'s ancestry check upgraded to reject a merge record commit (rev-list --parents, not bare rev-parse ^); 3g's merge call and MERGED wait now STRICT-STOP-guarded and bounded; _load_pin gained an isinstance(dict) guard. 2 findings explicitly deferred with written rationale rather than fixed: the R5a root-conflation finding (defers to R5a, which the doc already assigns this exact work), and pin()'s re-ship-defeats-the-overwrite-guard finding (defers to R4, state mechanics). The diff_head/fires portion of the concurrency finding was independently re-verified and found not to reproduce (both are consumed before the spawn boundary, not after) -- rebutted, not fixed. No high finding either round; the automated loop was never shown to merge an uncertified commit.
